title: Path orchestration quirk - investigation notebook
content:
Summary:
Quick scratchpad for a stubborn production incident where certain customer traffic from eu-west kept being steered to a pedagogical node pool in us-east for ~15–40s bursts. Symptoms were intermittent increased p95 for short requests and partial token drops on long streaming sessions.

High-level hypothesis so far:
- orchestration/steering hysteresis allowed a stale zone preference to persist after transient capacity blips (affinity decay too slow)
- NAT/egress mapping drift on the edge LB caused route evaluation to treat requests as coming from a different region cohort
- fallback policy election race: policy ejected origin but routing subsystem failed to rebind to local-compatible variant until timeout

What I observed (chronological breadcrumbs):
- 2026-02-10 03:18 UTC: first customer alert (app p95 spike 800ms -> 3.2s).
- 03:18:02: trace opened via jaeger (trace id 1f3a2d): routing.policy.eval logs show "cohort:eu-west, score:0.81" then a sudden "candidate:pool-us-east chosen (ttl 30s)".
- 03:18:04: client websocket stream shows sporadic 502/connection-reset from edge for a subset of sessions.
- 03:18:10: autoscale event on eu-west pool (scale-out started) — but traffic remained ejected for ~27s afterward.

Commands I ran / artifacts captured:
- kubectl logs -n routing svc/steering-controller -f | grep "candidate:pool-us-east"  (captured timestamps matching spike)
- tcpdump -i eth0 src host 10.4.12.33 and dst port 443 -w eu-west-traffic.pcap (saw SYNs routed through us-east NAT IP 52.203.12.9)
- curl -v https://edge-eu-west.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer <test-key>" -d '{"prompt":"hello"}'  (intermittent 503: upstream unavailable)
- redis-cli -h redis-rt01 MONITOR (observed a burst of route-binding:set entries then a cascade of deletes)
- iptables -t nat -S (no obvious static rules, confirmed conntrack active)
- sudo tc qdisc show dev eth0 (qdisc defaults; nothing shaping)
- rtrctl dump-affinities --region eu-west --recent (custom tool) -> saw entries with expiry set to +30s longer than expected after node-restart events

Representative log snippets:
- routing.policy: DEBUG eval request_id=aa3f1a cohort=eu-west candidates=[eu-west,aus-syd,us-east] selected=us-east reason="prefScoreDelta 0.62 > hysteresis 0.5"
- steering-controller: WARN bind-fallback request_id=aa3f1a timeout=30000ms electorate-race=true
- edge-proxy: ERROR upstream connectivity failure to 10.255.0.12:5042 (connection reset)

Replay steps to reproduce in staging (work-in-progress):
1) artificially inject a small packet/latency blip on eu-west pool (iptables -A INPUT -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.02 -j DROP)
2) hit the same session pattern (short priming request then streaming continuation) using loadgen that mimics client behavior (client ip pinned to eu-west CIDR via nat simulation)
3) tail steering-controller logs and run rtrctl dump-affinities to watch election and expiry behavior
4) simultaneously capture conntrack with sudo conntrack -L | grep <session-ip> to see NAT mapping lifecycle

Quick ideas and next tests (ordered):
- shorten steering hysteresis to 15000ms in a canary branch and run in staging to confirm quicker rebound to local pools.
- verify affinity expiry uses last-observed-origin rather than first-observed-origin (codewalk in steering-controller election logic).
- add extra tracing fields: chosen_candidate_ttl, affinity_origin_ip, egress_nat_ip to make postmortem mapping cleaner.
- add a guard: if selected candidate is cross-region and local pool has scaling-in-progress, prefer local candidate until scale-out completes or 2nd-fallback.
- check edge LB conntrack timeout settings — ephemeral port reuse can confuse route cohorting under heavy concurrency.

Stuff I don't think is root but worth noting:
- model-level KV cache misses — I saw occasional 404s in the model shard, but timings don't align with initial routing decision window.
- deployment rollout PR #2897 changed a scheduling flag but that was committed 3 days earlier and doesn't match the incident timestamps.

Open questions / unknowns:
- why did autoscale event not flip routing back faster? is there an explicit dependency in the policy that waits for node health to be 'stable' for 30s?
- is there staleness in the central affinity store replication (redis shard lag)? monitor replication offset during next incident.
- are there edge-level NAT session handoffs when a session is pinned to a particular egress IP and that egress is rebalanced?

Action items (assigning roughly):
- Maya: run hysteresis-canary in staging and capture 1h of synthetic traffic (ETA 2026-02-17).
- Jamal: add extra affinity fields to trace payloads and PR trace schema change (ETA 2026-02-18).
- Priya: check conntrack / egress NAT config with infra (file ticket PLT-1423) and run long-lived NAT drain test (ETA 2026-02-19).

Notes to self: keep this notebook chronological and dump raw trace excerpts here; avoid losing the jaeger trace ids. If it reoccurs, focus on the moment the steering decisionlogs flip candidate -> cross-region and check conntrack mapping at that same second.

Raw trace ids captured so far:
- 1f3a2d (2026-02-10 03:18:02 UTC)
- 5b9c77 (2026-02-10 03:45:14 UTC)

Recent commands/short helpers I wrote during debug (local scripts):
- scripts/collect-session-state.sh (gathers conntrack, iptables nat, redis affinity dump for a given client-ip)
- scripts/replay-steer.sh (replays a short session with chosen client-ip nat to emulate the drift)

End of scratchpad for now — will paste interesting log excerpts here as they appear.
